title: Morgan Stanley goes max overweight global stocks, sees 15% S&P 500 upside on AI capex
description: A maximum overweight call from a major house is a timely counterweight to the AI jitters around Nvidia and the QTS debt pullback. It could encourage dip-buying in tech and in the wider set of AI beneficiaries. The upgrades to Japan and Europe matter for flows. They support the Nikkei and Topix, already helped by a weak yen, and European stocks that have lagged the US AI trade. Morgan Stanley’s call for a slightly stronger dollar suggests the gains for non-US stocks are expected to come from earnings rather than currency moves. Gold bulls get some comfort from its backing for gold, but in the near term Fed pricing still dominates. --- Where others see cracks in the AI trade, Morgan Stanley sees a buying opportunity: valuations have reset, the spending cycle is intact, and the next winners will be the companies putting AI to work. Summary: Morgan Stanley recommends a maximum overweight on global equities, saying the AI capex cycle remains intact. It kept US equities overweight, upgraded Japan and Europe to overweight, and held emerging markets at neutral. The bank raised its S&P 500 target, implying roughly 15% upside. It expects a slightly stronger US dollar and favours investment-grade corporate bonds and gold. Strategists said valuations have pulled back enough to justify a pro-risk stance. They expect market leadership to spread beyond cloud vendors, with AI application revenue in focus by 2027. Morgan Stanley has moved to its most bullish stance on global equities. It recommends a maximum overweight, on the view that the artificial intelligence investment cycle remains intact and will support economic growth and corporate earnings into next year, according to a report from Jinshi Data. In a note dated November 15, the bank’s strategists kept US equities at overweight, upgraded Japanese and European stocks to overweight and left emerging markets at neutral. They also raised their S&P 500 target, implying roughly 15% upside from current levels. The call rests partly on valuations. The strategists said the recent pullback in risk assets has made prices more attractive, prompting them to lean into risk rather than away from it. They also see market leadership broadening beyond the cloud computing giants that have driven much of the AI rally, and expect investors to focus more and more on revenue from companies deploying AI applications as 2027 approaches. Across other asset classes, Morgan Stanley expects a slightly stronger US dollar and favours investment-grade corporate bonds and gold. The timing gives the call added weight. It comes as investors weigh fresh questions over the AI trade. These include leadership turmoil at Nvidia ahead of its results on Tuesday, and signs of resistance in AI debt markets after Blackstone-backed data center operator QTS cut a planned private debt sale by about 60%. A Fed that is still raising rates is another headwind for valuations. The gold view also stands out. Morgan Stanley’s preference for bullion contrasts with Goldman Sachs, which over the weekend trimmed its end-2027 gold forecast to $4,650 an ounce on expectations of further Fed hikes. Gold is trading near $3,876 in Asia. For equity investors, the key question is whether AI spending keeps flowing through to earnings as financing costs rise. Morgan Stanley is betting that it will, and that the next leg of gains will come from the companies putting AI to work, not only from those building the infrastructure. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.
